fieldMarks: Large grouse with a long, spiky tail.
Male: white breast contrasting with a black bib and black belly; two yellow air sacs inflated in display.
Female: plainer, told by large size, long tail and dark belly patch.
behavior: Males display on traditional leks, puffing the white chest, inflating air sacs and fanning the tail with loud pops and bubbling sounds.
Flushed birds give a chicken-like cackle.
Eats mostly sagebrush leaves and shoots, plus flowers, buds and summer insects.
Largely non-migratory, with local movements out of high valleys in winter.
habitat: Sagebrush plains, high valleys, mesas and foothills; found only near sagebrush and needs access to water.
range: Sagebrush regions of the western US and western Canada; it has disappeared from much of its former range.

lookalikes.name: Gunnison sage-grouse
lookalikes.howToTell: Gunnison is smaller, with bolder pale tail bars, a longer head plume and a different display; their ranges do not overlap.
